content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in the short term, especially after bullish sentiment spikes.", "Sentiment indicators show strong correlation with price volatility, particularly when bullish sentiment exceeds 1.00.", "Model forecasts exhibit mean-reversion bias when official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates.", "Price overshoots are more likely when recent auction supply events are high and sentiment is mixed.", "Forecast accuracy improves when bullish sentiment is low and supply net is minimal.", "Model bias is amplified during periods of high event frequency and negative supply net.", "Sentiment shifts should trigger model recalibration if price divergence exceeds 5% from forecast.", "Forecast lag is significant when official events are sparse and sentiment remains stable."]}
